subject: Clarify invoice submission flow & long-format invoice BCC routing
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@lumenworks.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LumenWorks Billing <accounts@lumenworks.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: New vendor: question on invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Rishi,

We're completing the vendor onboarding (LumenWorks -> Redwood) and have a couple of questions about the invoice intake preferences so we can automate our AP workflow:

- We saw a portal option in the vendor onboarding email, but we still often Bcc a central AP inbox for remittance. Which method should we rely on so invoices are processed fastest?
- Our invoices sometimes include a long "PO line details" multi-page PDF plus a CSV of line items. Does the portal accept both PDF + CSV attachments, or should we attach the CSV only and paste the long memo text into the portal's "Notes" field?
- When we email invoices as a fallback, should we put the PO number in the subject line or in the email body? Any required filename structure?

We're attaching a sample invoice and our CSV export for a real example. Could you point us to the canonical mapping so we don't have to manually rework rows?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Billing Lead, LumenWorks
jordan.ellis@lumenworks.com
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachment: LumenWorks_INV_20261101.pdf (invoice PDF)
Attachment: lumenworks_invoice_lines.csv (CSV of line items)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@lumenworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New vendor: question on invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Jordan — great to hear from you and welcome aboard. Short answers up front, then details and a recommended fallback: 

1) Preferred path: portal first. Our portal ties Invoice -> PO -> GL mapping automatically and gives the fastest route to AP. Please use the portal for routine invoices.

2) Attachments: Portal accepts a single PDF invoice and an optional CSV for line-level import. If your CSV contains canonical line items we can ingest it, but the portal requires the CSV columns to match our sample mapping (see link below). The long-form supporting PDF should be uploaded as the invoice PDF; do not paste large multi-page text into the "Notes" field — notes are for short remittance instructions only.

3) Email fallback: If you must email, Bcc our centralized intake at ap-invoices@redwoodinference.com. Put the PO number in the Subject as: PO <PO_NUMBER> | Invoice <INVOICE_NUMBER>. This ensures our inbound parser tags the PO correctly. Filenames should include PO and invoice numbers if possible (e.g., PO12345_INV6789.pdf).

Workarounds and gotchas:
- If your CSV has nested line descriptions exceeding 255 chars we recommend you keep the detailed narrative in the PDF (supporting doc) and include a short summary in the CSV description column — the portal's CSV parser truncates long freeform fields.
- For multi-invoice PDFs (multiple invoices in one PDF) please upload one PDF per invoice to avoid processing delays.

Action items I can take now:
- Ben (cc'd) will validate your attached CSV against our mapping and reply with a quick diff of required column headers.
- Marissa will add a one-page vendor-facing cheat sheet with the exact filename/subject pattern and a CSV sample so your AP team can export to the right schema.

Link: Vendor onboarding CSV spec — https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b-onboarding-form (portal CSV sample)

If you'd like, we can schedule a 20-minute screen-share to walk your AP person through a test upload.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Vendor Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Can you confirm whether we should split the long description into a separate support attachment or map it to a portal 'supporting_document' field? Also, do you want us to Bcc ap-invoices@redwoodinference.com on those email uploads for faster routing?

Attaching the same two files again.

- Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: New vendor: question on invoice submission (portal vs email)

Hi Jordan — thanks for the test upload and the CSV excerpt. Confirming a few practical rules so your AP can automate without manual steps: 

- CSV field behavior: the portal's CSV schema truncates description fields to 512 characters. For longer narrative, please put the full narrative in the supporting PDF and include a short 1-2 sentence summary in the CSV description column. We will not drop the PDF; it will be linked to the invoice record for review.

- Supporting document mapping: use the CSV column 'supporting_doc_filename' (see the sample CSV) to name the PDF. The portal will attach the PDF to the matching invoice record if the filenames match. This avoids copying large text into portal note fields.

- Email fallback: yes, Bcc ap-invoices@redwoodinference.com on emailed invoices. Use subject pattern: PO <PO_NUMBER> | INV <INVOICE_NUMBER>. That ensures our inbound parser tags the PO and routes it through the same workflow as portal-submitted invoices.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa: will upload a one-page vendor cheat sheet to the Drive link and email it to Jordan's accounts alias by EOD tomorrow.
- Rishi: will monitor the first 2-3 invoices to confirm mapping/auto-match rates and follow up if we see a >10% manual-match rate.

If helpful I can also provide a small Python snippet to convert your current CSV export to our schema — happy to drop that into the Drive folder.

Regards,
Ben Carter
AP Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
